summary: Frontend E2E verification of the LIVE (non-mock) Razorpay Standard Checkout integration. Logged in as testagent2026@gmail.com (paid=false), navigated directly to /session/10c9e2ec-ee33-4b2c-987a-eae4b40ed8c6/start, verified the full paywall -> create-order -> Razorpay checkout iframe flow end-to-end. All critical pieces pass. The 'infinite loading spinner' reported by main agent was a false alarm — the SessionPaymentGate's payment-gate-loading spinner correctly shows for ~5s while /api/payments/eligibility resolves, then transitions to the paywall modal. Not a bug.

action_items: No fixes required. The 'infinite loading spinner' the main agent observed was simply the ~5s cold-start latency of /api/payments/eligibility. Consider a UX tweak (spinner + text like 'Checking access…' or a max-wait timeout with retry) if you want to make cold starts less alarming, but this is not a functional bug.
OPTIONAL: The (now-unreachable) mock-mode branch and mock-success endpoint could be gated behind an env flag or removed to reduce dead code, since RAZORPAY_KEY_ID is now permanently set.
critical_code_review_comments: usePaymentFlow.jsx / PaywallModal.jsx: onSuccess handler uses window.location.reload() — this works but a soft re-fetch of eligibility would give a smoother post-payment UX.

SessionPaymentGate.jsx: on eligibility fetch error, sets data:null which then falls through to render children — this means a transient network blip could briefly show gated content before the next check. Minor; consider defaulting to a retry-with-error state instead.

SessionPaymentGate.jsx encodes an empty string when sessionId is undefined; server currently tolerates this, but adding a guard `if (!sessionId) return children;` would avoid a wasted request on non-session-scoped routes if this component ever gets reused.

rca_of_the_issue: Main agent's reported 'infinite loading spinner' when navigating to /session/{id}/start was not a real bug. Root cause: the SessionPaymentGate initial render shows a full-screen spinner (data-testid=payment-gate-loading) while awaiting /api/payments/eligibility. On a cold backend hit, this takes ~5 seconds. If a user (or an automated test) only waits 1–3 seconds and screenshots, it appears frozen. In this test, the spinner resolved cleanly within ~5-6s and the paywall rendered correctly. Mitigation (optional UX polish, not a bug fix): add label text 'Checking access…' under the spinner and/or a 10s timeout with a Retry button so the state is legible during slow eligibility responses.
